name: Supplier Performance Scorecard
summary: Scores and ranks suppliers on weighted metrics (on-time delivery, defects, lead time, cost) with explicit weights and direction.
description: Reads your supplier metrics with their weights and whether higher or lower is better, and each supplier's values, then normalises every metric across suppliers, applies the normalised weights and ranks suppliers on a 0-100 score. Missing values are excluded rather than scored as worst, and each supplier shows how much of the weight it was judged on. Vendor Evaluation Scorecard compares vendors qualitatively from notes; this one calculates from measured data. Who it's for: procurement, operations and supply chain managers running supplier reviews. Limitations: scores are relative to the suppliers compared, so adding a supplier changes everyone's score; it uses the figures you provide and does not adjust for volume or risk.
problems: Rank our suppliers on delivery, quality and cost
I need a weighted supplier scorecard
Which supplier performs best on our metrics

inputs.label: Metrics and weights
inputs.description: Each metric: name, weight, and whether higher or lower is better.
inputs.example:
On-time delivery % (higher is better), weight 50
Defect rate % (lower is better), weight 30

inputs.label: Supplier data
inputs.description: Each supplier with its value for every metric; leave out values you don't have.
inputs.example:
Alpha: on-time 98, defects 1.0
Beta: on-time 90, defects 0.5

outputs.label: Calculated results
outputs.description: Results with units, formulas, assumptions and warnings, from the registered calculation.

outputs.label: Explanation
outputs.description: What the results mean, with numbers taken only from the calculation.

execution.system: You are an analyst explaining calculated results to a business decision-maker. Be concrete and brief.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on what the results mean for the decision, using only calculated numbers.
summary.title: Summary

text.description: One point. Numbers only from the calculated results.

steps.name: Read your data
steps.responsibility: Copy your figures into the calculation's input exactly as written.
steps.prompt: Read each metric with a snake_case id, its name, weight, direction (higher_is_better or lower_is_better) and unit, then each supplier with its value for each metric id (null if not given). Copy numbers exactly.

steps.name: Calculate
steps.responsibility: Runs the registered supplier_scorecard@1 calculation. All numbers in the result come from here.

steps.name: Explain
steps.responsibility: Explains the calculated results; adds no numbers of its own.
steps.prompt: Explain the ranking, what drives each supplier's score, and where missing data limits the comparison. Mention every warning.

steps.name: Check explanation
steps.responsibility: Every number in the explanation matches the calculated results or your inputs.

criteria.description: Every number in the summary comes from the calculation or your inputs.
Every number in the key points comes from the calculation or your inputs.
The summary is 90 words or fewer.
